name: Scale-Split Dual-Operator Constraint-First (SSDC-MOND)
claimed_mechanism: This architecture employs a scale-split dual-operator strategy: a spatially nonlocal auxiliary chi enforces the MOND constraint at large scales (galactic), while a local algebraic scalar s mediates a screened preferred-frame screw term. The s-field couples to the acceleration u_mu with a coefficient that is exponentially screened by e^-y, ensuring the preferred-frame effects vanish in the Solar System. Crucially, the kinetic normalization of the vector field u_mu is independent of the screening factor, thereby decoupling the PPN response from the kinetic term and avoiding the P7 strong-coupling wall.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the nonlocal chi field generates the correct MOND force law (G1) without introducing propagating modes. The local s-field generates a PPN slip (gamma != 1) that is exactly proportional to e^-y, vanishing as y -> infinity. The tensor sector remains GR (c_T=1, Q_T>0) because the s-field is algebraic and does not modify the tensor kinetic term. The lensing ratio is corrected to the MOND value (eta=1) by the off-ray contribution of the s-field, evading the DC-013 slip-lock.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is distinct from DC-010 (khronometric) because it uses a spatially nonlocal operator for the MOND constraint rather than a local khronon field, and it employs a dual-operator scale-split structure. It is distinct from DC-012 (scale-split frameless) because it includes a preferred-frame coupling (s_screw) that is screened by e^-y, which is required to evade the DC-013 slip-lock. It is distinct from DC-014 (stiff vector) because the vector field u_mu has standard kinetic terms, not degenerate/stiff, and its kinetic normalization is independent of the screening factor. It is distinct from DC-001 (local no-frame) because it includes a preferred-frame coupling and a spatially nonlocal operator.
